anomalies.observed: Both ground pins on each isolated CAN transceiver are connected to the same GND net, bypassing the isolation barrier.
anomalies.expected: For the specified isolated CAN interfaces, each transceiver's GND1 and GND2 must remain on separate ground domains.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver (U11/companion)

anomalies.impact: The CAN interfaces lose galvanic isolation, allowing ground differences and transients on the external CAN wiring to couple into the board's logic ground.

parsed.summary: An anomaly is present: both CAN transceivers have their primary and isolated-side grounds tied to the same GND net. This defeats the galvanic isolation specified for the CAN interfaces.
